subject.title: Feature/Fix: Add conservative lineage safety and promotion controls

question: Should CodexBar adopt this four-PR lineage-accounting architecture, or first prefer the narrower fork-identity and cache-invalidation repair in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118?
rationale: Both approaches target the linked overcount, but they differ substantially in scope, accounting model, cache behavior, rollout complexity, and long-term maintenance cost.

options.title: Prefer narrow repair first
options.body: Land the smaller proven identity/cache repair and reassess whether the full lineage subsystem remains necessary for unresolved corpus cases.

options.title: Adopt lineage stack
options.body: Review and land the four PRs in dependency order after exact-head frozen-corpus proof covers promotion, containment, failure handling, and rollback.

options.title: Pause accounting changes
options.body: Retain current-main containment while maintainers define the permanent cross-file accounting model.

recommendation.title: Prefer narrow repair first
recommendation.body: Land the smaller proven identity/cache repair and reassess whether the full lineage subsystem remains necessary for unresolved corpus cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the architecture of the repository's central usage scanner and the long-term authority for displayed Codex totals.
